title: Cross-architecture embedding + reranker certification and pinned profile publishing
creator: Aisha Chen
description: Add support and certification workflow for publishing pinned performance profiles for embedding and pairwise reranker models across CPU x86_64, ARM64, and GPU (CUDA) variants. Deliverables: a reproducible benchmark suite, pinned profile metadata schema, automated profile publisher, and a rollout plan that ensures safe canarying for customers on Hosted and Dedicated. This ticket focuses on cross-architecture validation and producing the canonical pinned profiles that will be consumed by catalog and rollout systems.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark harness runs deterministically across x86_64, arm64, and CUDA instances and produces comparable metrics (throughput P50/P95, token cost, memory footprint) with seed reproducibility
Pinned profile JSON schema validated and stored in catalog with immutable version tags and documented checksum
Automated publisher can create a canary profile and trigger catalog rollout with a single command and a dry-run mode
Canary gating rules are in place: difference thresholds for P95 latency, token cost, and quality delta against control model
Integration tests exercising model selection fallbacks (quantized <-> fp16) pass on CI for all three architectures
technical_notes: We need to capture warmup behavior: first-request latency vs steady-state throughput (continuous batching impacts)
Quantized variants show 10-18% lower memory but can increase tail latency under high concurrent KV cache pressure
ARM64 has slightly different kernel scheduling; add scale factor normalizers in the profile metadata to account for measured divergence
Use deterministic seed for synthetic request generator; record RNG seeds used for each run in artifacts
decisions: Schema: use top-level fields 'profile_version', 'arch', 'variant', 'seq_buckets', 'metrics' and include a 'calibration' block for cross-arch multipliers
Storage: pinned profiles are immutable once published; updates require publishing new profile_version and linking as supersedes
Canary policy: run canary on 5% of traffic for 24 hours, require no more than 10% regression in P95 and <2% quality delta to promote
Publishing flow: automated verification -> dry-run -> create canary -> monitor 24h -> promote or rollback
tasks: Add ARM64 CI job that provisions a small instance and runs benchmark harness (Liam)
Extend benchmark harness to emit per-bucket metrics and deterministic seeds (Aisha)
Implement profile publisher CLI with --dry-run and --force flags (SRE pairing)
Wire pinned profile storage into catalog service and add checksum verification (Platform team)
Create canary monitoring dashboard with SLO/quality alerting and automated rollback hook (Observability)
Update onboarding doc for model ops to include cross-arch checklist and acceptance steps (Docs)
Run three full certification passes on representative models (embedding-small, reranker-base, reranker-large) and upload artifacts
